title: Polish Independence Day: 11 November and Its Traditions
excerpt: Polish Independence Day on 11 November: why 1918 matters, how the holiday was banned and restored, and Poznań's St Martin's croissant.
metaDescription: Polish Independence Day on 11 November explained: the 1918 story, 123 years of partitions, how Poles celebrate today, St Martin's croissant and key vocab.
summary: Polish Independence Day on 11 November marks the day in 1918 when Józef Piłsudski took command of the Polish army after 123 years of partitions.
The communists abolished the holiday in 1945 and replaced it with 22 July; the Sejm restored 11 November in February 1989.
Today Poles mark it with state ceremonies at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, flags, independence runs, concerts and marches.
In Poznań, 11 November is also St Martin's Day, celebrated with the EU-protected rogal świętomarciński filled with white poppy seeds.
